deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page belongs to Gauss's dioptric computations for an achromatic double objective. The design has a crown lens followed by a flint lens, and each lens is a meniscus. 'Hypothesis I' is one trial set of radii. The previous page ('Nro 3') runs the same scheme with other radii. The next page traces finite (trigonometric) rays at edge and middle ('Rand', 'Mitte') to study spherical aberration. This page is the paraxial (axial) part: it follows a parallel axial bundle through four surfaces for three colours, using 7-place logarithms (negative characteristics written +10).

DATA (decoded from the logs).
- Crown indices: log n = 0.1773483, 0.1804591, 0.1835477, so n = 1.50435, 1.51516, 1.52598. The log(n-1) values 9.7027303, ... agree.
- Flint indices: log n' = 0.1991543, 0.2046002, 0.2099785, so n' = 1.58181, 1.60177, 1.62173. The log(n'-1) values 9.7647812, ... agree.
- Radii: log r = 1.5808565 gives r = 38.094; log r' = 2.1624458 gives r' = 145.360; log r'' = 1.6792472 gives r'' = 47.780; log r''' = 1.4875112 gives r''' = 30.726. The next page confirms 38.09399, 145.3603, 47.78012, 30.72637.
- Top-left block: 2.4360720 minus 0.8552155 gives 1.5808565 (log r). Minus 0.2736262 gives 2.1624458 (log r'). Minus 0.7568248 gives 1.6792472 (log r''). So the radii are a common length (10^2.436072 = 272.95) divided by 7.1647, 1.8777 and 5.7120. Presumably these are the radii of a normalised design scaled to this focal length. log r''' = 1.4875112 is written below the line because it is determined later on the page. The figures '0008951' and the struck '9491049' are unclear.

FORMULAS (top right). Refraction at a spherical surface, written with signed vergences:
- Entry (Eintritt): 1/α = 1/(a n) - (n-1)/(n f).
- Exit (Austritt): 1/α = n/a + (n-1)/f = (n-1)(n/(n-1)·1/a + 1/f).
- Rearranged variants: 1/α + 1/(a n) = (n-1)/(n f), hence n/((n-1)α) + 1/((n-1)a) = 1/f; also n/α + 1/a = (n-1)/f.
These are the same law under different sign conventions for a, α and f. Gauss uses whichever form makes the logarithmic work convenient.

COMPUTATION.

(1) Crown, first surface, parallel light in:
- α1 = r·n/(n-1).
- log(n/(n-1)) = 0.4746180, 0.4685153, 0.4625818. Adding log r gives α1 = 113.62516, 112.03966, 110.51934.
- Subtracting the crown thickness 2 gives a2 = 111.62516, 110.03966, 108.51934 (logs 2.0477624, 2.0415493, 2.0355072).

(2) Crown, second surface, in the form 1/((n-1)α) = n/((n-1)a) - 1/r':
- n/((n-1)a2) = 0.026721196, 0.026727970, 0.026734657.
- 1/r' = 0.006879457.
- The differences have logs 8.2975797, 8.2977274, 8.2978743.
- Adding colog(n-1) = 0.2972697, ... gives α2 = 99.92865, 97.79773, 95.75462.
- Subtracting the air gap 0.5 gives a3 = 99.42865, 97.29773, 95.25462. The crown alone is strongly chromatic (spread of about 4.2).

(3) Flint, first surface, in the form n'/((n'-1)α) = 1/((n'-1)a) + 1/r'':
- colog(n'-1) = 0.2352188, ...; log a3 = 1.9975116, ...
- 1/((n'-1)a3) = 0.017286504, 0.017079173, 0.016885432.
- 1/r'' = 0.020929207. The sums have logs 8.5822419, 8.5798793, 8.5776599.
- Adding log(n'/(n'-1)) = 0.4343731, 0.4251697, 0.4163767 gives α3 = 71.14284, 70.03102, 68.97898.
- Subtracting the flint thickness 0.8 gives a4 = 70.34284, 69.23102, 68.17898 (logs 1.8472199, 1.8403007, 1.8336505).

(4) Choice of r''' for achromatism (bottom left):
- Exit law: 1/α = n'/a - (n'-1)/r'''.
- Requiring equal final vergence for colours 1 and 3 gives 1/r''' = (n'3/a4,3 - n'1/a4,1)/(n'3 - n'1).
- n'1/a4,1 = 0.02248715 and n'3/a4,3 = 0.02378636. The difference is 0.00129921 (log 7.1136793).
- n'3 - n'1 = 0.039920 (log 8.6011905).
- Hence log r''' = 8.6011905 - 7.1136793 = 1.4875112, i.e. r''' = 30.726. This is the value entered at top left.

(5) Flint, last surface, in the form 1/((n'-1)α) = n'/((n'-1)a4) - 1/r''':
- n'/((n'-1)a4) = 0.03865037, 0.03844758, 0.03825835.
- 1/r''' = 0.03254534.
- The final focal distances behind the last surface are 281.5359, 281.5481, 281.5355.
- Colours 1 and 3 coincide by construction. The middle colour is about 0.012 longer: the residual secondary spectrum of Hypothesis I.

(6) Unexplained figures. The right-margin columns (1.03514/10.843, 1.03126/10.746, 1.02548/10.604, 1.01733/10.407) and the small scribbles at the bottom are auxiliary figures. I cannot interpret them with certainty.
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the checked chain. I recomputed: n/(n-1)·r = 113.625; 0.026721196 - 0.006879457 = 0.019841739 (log 8.2975797); α2 = 99.9287; 1/((n'-1)·99.42865) = 0.0172865; 0.0172865 + 0.0209292 (log 8.58224); α3 = 71.1428; log r''' = 1.4875112; final focal distances about 281.534 / 281.54 / 281.535. Small last-digit differences in my recomputation come from rounding the indices.
The scratch formulas at right mix sign conventions. '1/α + 1/(an) = (n-1)/(nf)' is the entry law with a's sign reversed relative to the boxed formula. This is a convention change, not an error.
The line transcribed '1/α + 1/(an) = n/(nf)' cannot be a correct refraction law as written. The numerator is presumably n-1 (a misreading or a slip).

results.what: Paraxial refraction at a spherical surface, n/α - 1/a = (n-1)/r, in several sign forms. It is applied surface by surface with thicknesses (2, 0.5, 0.8) to trace an axial bundle through a thick crown–flint doublet for three colours by logarithms.
results.modern_name: Paraxial (Gaussian) ray trace / vergence equation through a thick lens system
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Huygens, Newton, Cotes, Smith, Lagrange). The systematic thick-system theory is Gauss, Dioptrische Untersuchungen (1841).

results.what: Choice of the last radius r''' so that the extreme colours (indices n'1, n'3) have identical focal distances: 1/r''' = (n'3/a3 - n'1/a1)/(n'3 - n'1). The middle colour then shows a residual of about +0.012 in 281.5.
results.modern_name: Achromatization of a doublet (two-colour correction) with residual secondary spectrum

results.what: Design of an objective made of two menisci (crown positive meniscus r = 38.09, r' = 145.36; flint negative meniscus r'' = 47.78, r''' = 30.73), examined under trial 'hypotheses' together with finite-ray traces on the adjacent pages.
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss, 'Über achromatische Doppelobjective', Zeitschrift für Astronomie 4 (1817)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a numerical worksheet for Gauss's known two-meniscus achromatic objective (published 1817). The paraxial trace and two-colour achromatization are standard. The value lies in documenting his trial radii and the size of the secondary spectrum, not in any new result.
